# The History of the Roman Empire

## Origins and the Roman Kingdom (753–509 BCE)

Rome's legendary founding in 753 BCE is attributed to Romulus and Remus, twin brothers raised by a she-wolf. The early Roman Kingdom was ruled by seven kings, blending Etruscan, Latin, and Sabine influences into a unique culture. In 509 BCE, the monarchy fell, replaced by the Roman Republic following the overthrow of King Tarquin the Proud.

## The Roman Republic (509–27 BCE)

The Republic introduced governance through elected consuls, the Senate, and popular assemblies. Roman expansion began through conquest of the Italian peninsula, followed by the Punic Wars against Carthage (264–146 BCE). Hannibal's brilliant campaigns nearly destroyed Rome, but Scipio Africanus defeated him at Zama. conquests brought immense wealth through provinces like Sicily, Spain, and Greece. Social tensions between patricians and plebeians led to the Struggle of the Orders, gradually expanding plebeian rights. The late Republic saw figures like Julius Caesar, whose crossing of the Rubicon in 49 BCE sparked civil war. His assassination in 44 BCE led to decades of conflict, culminating in Augustus's rise to power.
